{{Quote|Star Tours welcomes you to our Tomorrowland Starport, the most modern and technologically advanced terminal in the universe.|Star Tours announcer|<ref name="TDL No14">{{YouTube|video=Bxy4eeyymug|text=TDL : Star Tours Queue Line No14|channel=@couperin9|name=couperin9}}</ref>}}
'''Tomorrowland Starport''' was a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] used by the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency.<ref name="ST1" />

==Layout==
[[File:Star_Tours_Maintenance_Area_Starlog119.jpg|thumb|250px|A maintenance area in the starport.]]
The Tomorrowland Starport was a massive complex which was divided into multiple areas: the Hangar, the Maintenance Bay, the [[Droidnostics Center]], the Boarding Concourse, the [[Outer Rim Concourse]],<ref name="TDL No1">{{YouTube|video=bTHFWK8G_7A|text=TDL : Star Tours Queue Line No1|channel=@couperin9|name=couperin9}}</ref> and the Baggage Claim for those who have arrived at the Starport.<ref name="ST1" />

Ramps from the hangar led to boarding areas, but passed directly through often messy droid repair areas in the Droidnostics Center. Signage in the spaceport was typically written in [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]], with other alphabets and languages used occasionally.<ref name="ST1" />

===Hangar===
The [[Hangar/Legends|Hangar]] was large enough to fit and service two [[StarSpeeder 3000]]s, and contained lifts for ease of access during repair work on the [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. In large part to impress passengers, the Hangar also acted as the departure lobby. The Hangar also contained several monitors throughout, which displayed the flight information such as destinations to and arrivals from various vacation destination [[Planet/Legends|planets]], and also gave the weather forecasts for each planet.<ref name="ST1" />

The [[Spacecap Droid]] [[F-25-OJSx]] was responsible for placing checked bags onto the baggage conveyor, with the various luggage also containing several unique decals. A fan was also present in the Hangar with [[F-22-RGKx]] supposed to work on maintaining it.<ref name="Complete Guide">''[[Complete Guide to Star Tours]]''</ref>

===Maintenance Bay===
[[File:StarSpeeder_3000.jpg|thumb|right|250px|R2-D2 with a StarSpeeder in the Maintenance Bay]]
The Maintenance Bay was where [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] worked on maintaining various StarSpeeders during their time with Star Tours in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="ST1" /> The bay included a status board containing 105 liquid crystal panels, with each panel measuring 30x30 centimeters. It advertised various destinations, including [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], [[Endor]], and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It also had three language settings for announcements, including [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]].<ref name="Complete Guide" />

The control booth in the bay was used to direct various operations within the starport, and was manned by at least two [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] supervisors. [[Spark jar]]s, the fuel for the StarSpeeder 3000, were located within the middle of the maintenance bay.<ref name="Complete Guide" />

===Droidnostics Center===
{{Main|Droidnostics Center}}
The Droidnostics Center was where droids were dispatched to be repaired before being sent back to work, and was largely unmanned. The droid foreman was [[G2-4T]].<ref name="ST1" /> [[Max-W 100]] and [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]] were workers at the area, although the latter tended to goof off, max-W 100 was dedicated to his work.<ref name="Complete Guide" /> At least one area of the center was Sector 2.<ref name="ST1" />

===Boarding Concourse===
[[File:Startours-security.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Mon Calamari security officer observing the concourse]]
The Boarding Concourse was one of the few places where human Star Tours crew members were seen. It acted as the final destination before boarding an StarSpeeder 3000 and contained six boarding gates. At least one boarding concourse had all six boarding gates dedicated to Endor as part of the [[Endor Express]]. Flight monitors also showcased via onboard cameras the current status of a StarSpeeder 3000 as well as the amount of time before departure.<ref name="ST1" />

===Baggage Claim===
The Baggage Claim was filled with baggage conveyors. The [[PanaRobo]] droids [[P-6]] and [[S-4]] inspected the incoming astrocultural freight under an [[Quarantine supervisor R2 unit|R2 unit's]] supervision, and disinfected the baggage with a spray and a flyswatter. Nearby was the [[Tourscan]], a display screen narrated by [[Dan Android]] that supplied advertisements for various vacation packages. The area included a [[Star*Link]] booth, which was frequently used by [[F-29-PSKx]] to call [[Lady Droid|his girlfriend]] due to homesickness.<ref name="Complete Guide" />

==History==
Months after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], droid pilot [[RX-24/Legends|RX-24's]] [[Battle of Death Star III|near disastrous flight]] intended for the [[Endor/Legends|forest moon]] started and ended at this spaceport. The station also contained some [[fuel truck]]s which [[Star Tours Flight 45|ST-45]], RX-24's assigned StarSpeeder 3000 number, nearly crashed into upon arriving back at the spaceport.<ref name="ST1" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tomorrowland_schematics.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Schematics of Tokyo's Tomorrowland Starport]]
{{Quote|Hello, I am C-3PO, and this is my counterpart, R2-D2. Welcome to the Star Tours Tomorrowland Spaceport!|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] announcement on Disneyland PeopleMover|<ref name="ST1" />}}
The term "Tomorrowland Starport" was only used in the queues of [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']] attractions in California's [[Disneyland]] and [[Tokyo Disneyland]], since they are in those parks' Tomorrowland areas, with the Tokyo version being part of an expansion called the Tomorrowland Astrozone.<ref name="DNM 2">{{BookCite|container=Crafting a Cast of Characters: The Art of Sculpture at Imagineering|title=Disney News Magazine|version=vol. 28|number=no. 2|date=Spring 1993|link=https://archive.org/details/DisneyNewsMagazine_Vol28.2_1993.Spring/mode/2up}}</ref> It was not used at [[Disney's Hollywood Studios]] or [[Disneyland Paris]].

Though purportedly the same starport, the attraction's physical location at each park varies. Both the Hangar and Baggage Claim sections are only part of the queue and offloading areas at Tokyo Disneyland. Before entering the Maintenance Bay area, visitors of the Disneyland ride in California pass by a security booth occupied by a Mon Calamari. At that same park, the [[Wikipedia:PeopleMover|PeopleMover]] ride that took guests on a tour around Tomorrowland included a segment that drove through the ride building with a view of the queue, until that ride closed in [[1995]]. An announcement by C-3PO on that ride used the term Tomorrowland "Spaceport" instead of "Starport."<ref name="PeopleMover">{{YouTube|video=uEpHsJCjNXg|text=DISNEYLAND PEOPLEMOVER 1989|channel=UCUbL1rNWyuWqGJ01hFun7fg|name=Douglas Moore}}</ref>
